title: Coordinate Geometry: Distance and Section Formulae
seo_title: Coordinate Geometry Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_text: Concepts of coordinate geometry, graphs of linear equations; distance formula; section formula (internal division) (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Coordinate Geometry worksheet (NCERT Chapter 7): distance formula, equidistant points, collinearity, section formula, mid-points and trisection. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Section formula: ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m + n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m + n)).
body_html:
How it works

Distance formula: the distance between P(x₁, y₁) and Q(x₂, y₂) is √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]. From the origin: √(x² + y²).

Section formula: the point dividing PQ internally in the ratio m : n is ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m + n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m + n)).

Mid-point (ratio 1 : 1): ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).

Example

Find the distance between (2, 3) and (4, 1).

√[(4 − 2)² + (1 − 3)²]

√8

Answer: 2√2

Example

Find the point dividing A(4, −3) and B(8, 5) in the ratio 3 : 1.

x = (3 × 8 + 1 × 4)/4 = 7

y = (3 × 5 + 1 × (−3))/4 = 3

Answer: (7, 3)

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the square root in the distance formula.
  • Swapping m and n: m goes with the second point (x₂, y₂).
  • Adding the coordinates for the mid-point without dividing by 2.

faq.a: The distance between (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]. It comes from Pythagoras theorem.
The point dividing the join of (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) internally in the ratio m : n is ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m + n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m + n)).

faq.q: How do I check whether three points are collinear using distances?
faq.a: Find the three distances. If the two shorter ones add up to the longest, the points are collinear.

faq.q: How do I find the ratio in which the x-axis divides a segment?
faq.a: Take the ratio as k : 1 and set the y-coordinate from the section formula equal to 0, then solve for k.
